description: Why each setting is as it is: decisions/020-renovate.md
CI and Railway's build install an exact npm, because Node 24's bundled npm is older than .npmrc's engine-strict accepts.
tests/unit/config/renovate.test.ts checks this pattern matches every npm@<version> in ci.yml and .railway/railway.ts.
Next's TypeScript plugin and the type check in next build use TypeScript's in-process JS API, which TypeScript 7 does not ship.
Lift this when TypeScript 7 has a stable JS API that Next supports. See decisions/012-project-init.md.
Node's types follow the Node line the app runs on, which .nvmrc names.
Raise this together with .nvmrc when the app moves to a newer even-numbered Node.
A new Node major in .nvmrc waits for approval in the Dependency Dashboard.
Moving lines also means raising the @types/node hold, which tests/unit/config/renovate.test.ts ties to .nvmrc, so the two change together by hand.
Only even-numbered Node lines are proposed for .nvmrc: engines refuses 25, as jsdom does.
Every GitHub Actions update waits for approval in the Dependency Dashboard, after its release has been read.

The SonarCloud job runs checkout, setup-node and download-artifact on the same runner before its scan and gate steps receive SONAR_TOKEN, so any of them could reach it; the 14-day age alone does not stop a compromise found late.
